contributions: Survey of subgraph isomorphism algorithms including VF2
Explanation of classical frequent subgraph mining via anti-monotonicity and gSpan
Introduction of order embeddings for encoding partial orders in continuous space
Presentation of SPMiner as a neural approach for scalable subgraph frequency estimation
limitations: Exact subgraph isomorphism is NP-complete with O(n! * n) worst-case time complexity. Classical mining algorithms cannot overcome the exponential number of frequent patterns. SPMiner is an approximation that may produce false positives and negatives due to imperfect order embedding preservation and neighborhood decomposition. Single-graph support measures may fail anti-monotonicity, losing pruning ability.
methods: The chapter presents three methodological stages: (1) exact subgraph isomorphism via VF2 algorithm using depth-first search with pruning based on feasibility rules, (2) classical frequent subgraph mining using the Apriori/anti-monotonicity property with gSpan's canonical DFS code representation for pattern enumeration, and (3) neural frequency estimation via SPMiner, which uses a GraphSAGE GNN encoder to map graphs into order embedding space trained with max-margin loss, then estimates frequency by counting neighborhoods with near-zero order violation.
results: SPMiner estimates subgraph frequency in milliseconds for graphs with millions of nodes, compared to hours or days for exact VF2-based approaches. The order embedding approach trades exactness for speed, with false positives and negatives from imperfect order preservation and neighborhood decomposition introducing approximation error. Classical algorithms like gSpan achieve polynomial-time enumeration but face exponential pattern counts as a fundamental barrier.
tldr: This chapter covers frequent subgraph mining from classical combinatorial algorithms (VF2, gSpan) to neural approaches (SPMiner with order embeddings), enabling scalable identification of recurring graph patterns.
